# 2 Samuel 21 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 21 (22 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 7

---

## V.1 — "house of blood" vs. "bloodstained house"
- **EMET:** "the-house of-the-bloods [ha-damim]"
- **LOGOS:** "his house of blood"
- **PNEUMA:** "his bloodstained house"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his bloodstained house." PNEUMA captures the force of the plural *damim* most vividly.

---

## V.4 — "What are you saying?" vs. "What do you say?" vs. "Tell me what you want"
- **EMET:** "What [are]-you saying?"
- **LOGOS:** "What do you say?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Tell me what you want"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Tell me what you want, and I will do it for you." Combines PNEUMA's directness with the full Hebrew clause.

---

## V.9 — "fell together" vs. "died together"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "the seven of them fell together"
- **PNEUMA:** "All seven died together"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "All seven fell together." PNEUMA's "all seven" with EMET/LOGOS's "fell" (*naflu*).

---

## V.10 — "water was poured" vs. "rain fell" vs. "rains came pouring down"
- **EMET:** "water was-poured upon-them from the-heavens"
- **LOGOS:** "rain fell upon them from heaven"
- **PNEUMA:** "the rains came pouring down from the sky"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "rain poured upon them from heaven." Preserves the force of *nittakh* ("was poured") with natural English.

---

## V.16 — "said to strike" vs. "said he would strike" vs. "was about to kill"
- **EMET:** "he-said to-strike David"
- **LOGOS:** "said he would strike down David"
- **PNEUMA:** "He was about to kill David"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "intended to strike down David." More precise than the literal "said."

---

## V.17 — "helped him" vs. "came to his aid" vs. "rushed in"
- **EMET:** "helped-him Avishai"
- **LOGOS:** "Abishai came to his aid"
- **PNEUMA:** "Abishai rushed in"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "came to his aid" — LOGOS. PNEUMA's "rushed in" adds urgency not in *'azar*.

---

## V.1 — "bloodstained house" — additional note on scope
- **EMET:** "because he-killed the-Giv'onim"
- **LOGOS:** "because he put the Gibeonites to death"
- **PNEUMA:** "because he slaughtered the Gibeonites"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "because he put the Gibeonites to death." LOGOS's formal phrasing. PNEUMA's "slaughtered" intensifies beyond the Hebrew *hemit*.

---
*— SOPHIA*
